2c1eeb27c2: Yes. If the certificate ever changes unexpectedly, Audex stops and asks before connecting again.

8fae15159b: Privacy Policy for Audex, a self-hosted-first audio and audiobook player for Android.
993a2d7db1: This is a translation, provided for convenience. If it differs from the English version, the English version applies.
de1868522a: Audex is built around a simple principle: your media library and listening activity belong on your device, not on our servers. This policy explains, in plain language, what limited information Audex does handle, why, and the choices you have over it.
20fa2d3a9d: Your audio files, documents, playlists, and listening history are stored locally on your device.
6661a0be00: We do not run analytics, tracking, or advertising SDKs of any kind.
3786f4be62: We never sell your data or share it with advertisers.
5f2410fe77: Cloud storage (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, etc.) is accessed only with your explicit authorization, to fetch content you choose.
d18d514a83: Purchases are processed entirely by Google Play — we never see your payment details.
4c2f1d7043: If the app crashes, a technical crash report is sent automatically to help us fix it — you can turn this off at any time.
59491256ce: Audex is designed to minimize what ever leaves your device. The categories below cover everything we handle.
fa872d3b50: If you sign in with Google, we receive your name, email address, and account identifier from Google, solely to identify your account within the app. This is stored securely on your device.
3fce3722ff: Audio files, documents, playlists, listening progress, and app preferences are stored locally on your device. We do not upload, inspect, or have access to this content.
fd930a6953: If you choose to connect a cloud storage account (such as Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, or a self-hosted server) to import content, Audex accesses only what's needed to browse and retrieve the specific items you select. Any access credentials are stored securely on your device and are never sent to us.
e20de48c65: Purchases are handled entirely by Google Play and confirmed directly on your device through Google's own Play Billing system. We never receive your payment card, billing address, or any other financial or purchase detail on any server we operate.
ec0ea50566: If you sign in with Google, then to recognize your free trial consistently across reinstalls and devices signed into the same Google account, our servers store a minimal record tied to that account: an account identifier and the date your trial first began. This record does not include whether or when you've purchased Audex — that's determined entirely on your own device, directly from Google Play, each time the app checks.
82ddd0f735: We also retain a second, separate value: a one-way cryptographic hash of your account identifier, which cannot be reversed to reveal who it belongs to. Its only purpose is recognizing that a given account has already used a trial, even after the record above has been deleted — without it, deleting and recreating that record would let a trial be reset indefinitely. This hash carries no information about you or your activity beyond that one yes/no fact.
5594022f13: Signing in is optional, so the trial is also recognized per device, on your phone and on Android TV alike. For this, our servers store a one-way cryptographic hash of the device's Android ID (an identifier Android gives each app on each device; the hash cannot be reversed to reveal it) together with the date the trial began on that device. If you're also signed in, the earlier of the two dates applies to both. Like the hash above, this record is kept only so a trial can't be restarted by reinstalling the app or clearing its data, and nothing else about you or your activity is stored on our servers.
bb6b46d74f: If you submit a bug report or feature request, we receive the message you write along with basic app and device information (app version, device model, Android version) to help us respond. You may optionally choose to include a screenshot and a short excerpt of on-device diagnostic logs — these are only ever sent if you actively opt in for that specific report, and you can review exactly what will be sent before it's submitted.
36f2cfd16c: If Audex crashes on your phone, tablet, TV, or watch, a technical crash report is sent automatically so we can identify and fix the underlying bug. This report contains only a stack trace (which line of code failed and why) and basic app and device information (app version, device model, Android version). It never includes a screenshot, a copy of your on-device activity log, or the contents of your media library — on rare occasions, the stack trace itself may reference a local file or folder path if that's what the underlying error refers to, but it never includes what's inside that file. A crash on a paired Wear OS watch is relayed through your phone to reach us, since the watch has no direct internet connection of its own for this. Automatic crash reporting is on by default and can be turned off at any time in Settings on your phone or TV — turning it off on the phone also stops crash reports being sent on behalf of a paired watch.

4d107f9792: No method of storage or transmission is 100% secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security — but we design Audex to minimize what could ever be exposed in the first place, by keeping as little data as possible off your device.
186bc1a3f9: Depending on where you live, you may have rights to access, correct, or delete your personal information. In Audex, you can exercise most of these directly:
6b32ecc349: Delete local data: uninstall the app, or use the in-app options to clear your history or remove imported content. This takes effect immediately, without contacting us.
